title: Read the start years, and refuse what is not a schedule

blocks.text: A gas utility's planners run the main-replacement model every month and hand its answer to a reporting job. The job needs two things from each solve: every project's start year, and which funded projects were pushed past the first year they could start. It also must not report a schedule that is not one: last month a run stopped early and handed over values like 0.5, and the report rounded them into a plan nobody had approved.

items: `read_starts(values, projects, tol=1e-6)` takes the values the solver returned, `values[(pid, year)]`, one for each start variable, and returns every project's start year, or `None` for a project that is not funded. It raises `ScheduleError` when the values are not a schedule.
`deferrals(starts, projects)` returns, for each funded project that starts after its earliest allowed year, how many years later it starts.

blocks.text: In the lesson's notation, the solver returns a value $`\hat x_{i,t}`$ for each $`i \in P`$ and $`t \in T_i`$, and a solver only promises those values to within a tolerance $`\varepsilon`$ of the domain $`\{0, 1\}`$. Before you code, write down in that notation which values are a schedule (when is $`\hat x_{i,t}`$ read as 1, as 0, or as neither, and how many years of one project may read as 1), and what a project's start year $`s_i`$ and its deferral are in terms of $`\hat x_{i,t}`$ and $`\min T_i`$.
The tests hand your functions values directly, so no solver runs. About fifteen lines in total.

cases.says: every project is reported, with its start year if funded and None if not
a deferral is the number of years a funded project starts after its earliest allowed year
a value a tolerance away from 0 or 1 is read as that whole number
a value that is neither near 0 nor near 1 is refused rather than rounded
a project with two start variables at 1 is refused rather than given either year
a project that starts in its earliest year is not reported as deferred

origin.section: The Schedule Is Read Off the Variables That Are 1

concepts: the schedule is read from the start variables whose values are 1 within the solver's tolerance
